actions.action: Push a wooden chopstick to the bottom of the pot for 10 minutes to check soil moisture
Check whether the black pot is a cover pot without holes holding water
If soil is dry all the way down, water thoroughly
Move plant to sunniest (south-facing) window with blinds open
Alternatively put it outdoors in a sunny spot once nights stay above 5 °C
Alternatively set up a grow light 20–30 cm above it for 12–14 hours a day
Water when the chopstick is dry halfway down, until it drains
Empty the cover pot after each watering
If roots are soggy or mushy, repot into a slightly bigger pot with drainage holes and gritty mix (1/3 perlite)
Once in good light, cut leggy stems back by a third, wearing gloves

reason: The answer blames low light and overwatering, listing dryness only as an unlikely possibility, so the diagnosis is partial; the watering fix appears only as a conditional step, but the chopstick check guards against harm.
